issues.evidence: Tibetan 'འཇིག་རྟེན་བསམ་པ་བཏང་' ('jig rten bsam pa btang); bo-shenga 8-22 glosses it as abandoning 'འཇིག་རྟེན་པ་རྣམས་དང་འགྲོགས་པའི་བསམ་པ' (the intention of keeping company with worldly people), and bo-kunpal 8-22 as abandoning the worldly-accommodating intention. Sanskrit 'lokacintayā' is concern for the world. Hindi 'लोक के विचार' can be read as the thoughts held by the world.
issues.fix: इसलिए मैं लोक (लौकिक जनों) के साथ मेलजोल की चिन्ता/विचार को त्याग दूँगा

The line ends with a full-width CJK full stop (。) instead of a Devanagari-appropriate mark; stray punctuation, meaning intact.

Tibetan 'མགོ་སྙོམས་བྱེད་པ' (mgo snyoms byed pa) means to regard/treat as equal; bo-kunpal 8-29 glosses it as 'མགོ་སྙོམས་བྱེད' = equating one's own body with those skeletons ('འདི་དག་དང་འདྲའོ་ཞེས'), and bo-shenga as seeing one's body as of the same nature. Hindi 'समान करूँगा' reads as 'make equal' (a physical act), not 'regard as equal'.
issues.fix: कब मैं (उन्हें) समान मानूँगा / एक-सा देखूँगा?
